newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian inflation falls as trade balance improves.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian inflation falls as trade balance improves.

text.p: Annual inflation in Tanzania fell to 15.4 per cent in December -- down from 21.8 per cent at the end of 1995 -- while higher export earnings improved the trade balance, the country's central bank said on Sunday.
The inflation rate, reflected in the national consumer price index, fell from 16.2 per cent in November to 15.4 per cent in December, the monthly report showed.

"The decline... was mainly accounted for by a relatively low rate of inflation in the food group index which accounts for 71.2 per cent of the total weight in the consumer basket," the Bank of Tanzania (BOT) said.
Inflation was expected to fall further in January, given the bank's tight monetary and fiscal policies.
December's trade deficit, at $22 million, was down from $35.3 million in November, and the deficit for 1996 was $636.2 million against $857.9 million for 1995.

The bank said the "impressive performance" of traditional exports came from increased volume, not from higher prices. Exports of coffee, cotton, sisal, tobacco and cashew nuts all rose, while tea exports decreased by 1.9 per cent in value.

The bank commended the Tanzanian government's budgetary performance for the 1996/97 financial year, which began in July, with revenue collection, at 286.1 million shillings, representing 50.7 per cent of the budget for the year.
Revenue collection in December, at 61 million shillings, was a record, it added.
In contrast to other countries in the region which are facing serious drought, Tanzania expects good food crops, ensuring adequate food supplies up to the end of March, the report stated.
The food supply situation remained satisfactory in December with procurement for the Strategic Grain Reserve (SGR) totalling 58,243 tonnes, or .2 per cent above the target.
